scope.flow: Core::swap_6269342730() no-op swap path when sqrtRatio equals sqrtRatioLimit, skipping _updatePairDebtWithNative() while ETH was sent via msg.value
scope.environment: Core contract swap entrypoint invoked through Router with native ETH value

statements.text: The pool is initialized at tick 0 with liquidity.
The victim submits a swap with sqrtRatioLimit set near the current price for slippage protection, sending 10 ether as msg.value.
The attacker front-runs the victim's transaction and moves the price down to exactly the victim's sqrtRatioLimit.
Router calculates value = 10 ether and calls CoreLib::swap(), which sends 10 ETH to Core via call(gas(), core, value, ...).
The victim's swap transaction executes in Core::swap_6269342730() with stateAfter.sqrtRatio() equal to sqrtRatioLimit.
_updatePairDebtWithNative() is placed inside the conditional swap block that is skipped when sqrtRatio equals sqrtRatioLimit, so ETH sent via msg.value is never accounted for in the debt system.
When a swap is submitted with msg.value greater than zero, the sent ETH must be accounted for in the pair debt system rather than left unaccounted.
A swap that would be a no-op (sqrtRatio equal to sqrtRatioLimit) with msg.value greater than zero must not complete without accounting for the ETH; it should revert or otherwise handle the debt.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the victim's swap is the first transaction after pool initialization or whether prior swaps occurred.
The exact numeric sqrtRatioLimit value (tickToSqrtRatio(0-500)) is described only in the PoC, not as a general precondition.
Whether the attacker's front-run is required versus automatic price movement is presented as alternative triggers; the scenario uses the front-run variant.
Report does not specify the victim's authorization or any access control on swap; no permissionless-caller claim is made.
